source.author: verg
source.text: Eumenidum veluti demens videt agmina Pentheus, et solem geminum et duplicis se ostendere Thebas; aut Agamemnonius scaenis agitatus Orestes armatam facibus matrem et serpentibus atris cum fugit, ultricesque sedent in limine Dirae.
source.text_original: Eumenidum veluti demens videt agmina Pentheus, / et solem geminum et duplicis se ostendere Thebas; / aut Agamemnonius scaenis agitatus Orestes / armatam facibus matrem et serpentibus atris / cum fugit, ultricesque sedent in limine Dirae.
source.text_english: Just as Pentheus, mad, sees the bands of the Eumenides, and a twin sun and two Thebes appear before him; or as Agamemnon’s Orestes, driven through the stage, flees from his mother, armed with torches and black serpents, and the avenging Dirae sit on the threshold.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tu, nuntia sontum virgo Iovi, terras oculis quae prospicis aequis, ultricesque deae Fasque et grandaeva Furorum poena parens, meritis regis succedite tectis et saevas inferte faces.
reuse.text_original: tu, nuntia sontum / virgo Iovi, terras oculis quae prospicis aequis, / ultricesque deae Fasque et grandaeva Furorum / poena parens, meritis regis succedite tectis / et saevas inferte faces.
reuse.text_english: You, maiden, report the guilty to Jupiter; you who look out over the earth with impartial eyes, and you avenging goddesses and the Fates, and ancient mother of the punishment of the Furies, take possession of the king’s house as he deserves, and bring in your cruel torches.
